description: Northern Trust Corporation, a financial holding company, provides wealth management, asset servicing, asset management, and banking solutions for corporations, institutions, families, and individuals.
description_full: Northern Trust Corporation, a financial holding company, provides wealth management, asset servicing, asset management, and banking solutions for corporations, institutions, families, and individuals. It operates in two segments, Asset Servicing and Wealth Management. The Asset Servicing segment offers asset servicing and related services, including custody, fund administration, investment operations outsourcing, investment management, investment risk and analytics services, employee benefit services, securities lending, foreign exchange, treasury management, brokerage, transition management, banking, and cash management services. It serves corporate and public retirement funds, foundations, endowments, fund managers, insurance companies, sovereign wealth funds, and other institutional investors. The Wealth Management segment offers trust, investment management, custody, and philanthropic services; financial consulting; guardianship and estate administration; family business consulting; family financial education; brokerage; and private and business banking services. This segment also provides global custody, fiduciary services, family office consulting, and technology solutions to high-net-worth individuals and families, business owners, executives, professionals, retirees, and established privately held businesses. In addition, it offers asset management and related services comprising active and passive equity; active and passive fixed income; cash management; multi-asset and alternative asset classes that include private equity and hedge funds of funds; and multi-manager advisory services and products through separately managed accounts, bank common and collective funds, registered investment companies, exchange-traded funds, non-U.S. collective investment funds, and unregistered private investment funds. Further, the company provides overlay and other risk management services. The company was founded in 1889 and is headquartered in Chicago, Illinois.

CEO compensation is 11× revenue per employee (reasonable relative to workforce productivity). Governance score flags low compensation governance risk (2/10).
financial_summary: Northern Trust Corporation is a large-cap financial services business with a $31.3B market cap on $8.1B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +6% over the past three years and +6% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 13% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $5.5B in free cash flow — roughly 68 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 3.19× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.0× net debt/EBITDA, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 6.0% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome.

Low reinvestment-driven growth suggests the compounding engine has stalled
Piotroski score 4/9 — below the median for a healthy business

Credit cycles and regulatory capital — losses accumulate invisibly in good years and appear all at once, and the time to worry is when underwriting standards are loosest.
Fintech disintermediation — neobanks, embedded finance, and blockchain rails are unbundling the fee streams that traditional banks took for granted.
Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.

Market is pricing in lower growth than the company has historically delivered
39 consecutive years of dividend payments — an operating record that makes the dividend claim credible
Healthy payout ratio leaves room for both dividend growth and reinvestment
Minimal goodwill on the balance sheet — low impairment risk

sect: Its 29% operating margin is roughly in line with the Financial Services median (29%).
Its share of sector profits slightly exceeds its share of revenue (1.12x).
It accounts for 0.2% of sector revenue and 0.2% of sector operating profit.
Over five years it has been losing share of the sector profit pool (-3.8% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.02 across 512 companies in the universe; the top four hold 20% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 35% over the past year excluding the latest month, though it has pulled back 6% over the last three months.
The price sits mid-way through its 52-week range, 12% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 25% and a beta of 1.09, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.63 vs 5y 1.10), so read it loosely.
Liquidity is deep, with about $181.5M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 43% in the 2020 crash, 41% in the 2022 bear market and 60% in 2008.
val: The stock trades 57% below its DCF fair value of $403, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 33%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $298 to $552 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks cheap against Financial Services peers: P/FCF 5.7 vs 12.9 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 58% above its 10-year median.
The 14 covering analysts target $182 on average, 5% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 3.6% annual cash-flow growth, 16pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 13% earns above the cost of capital of 10.2%, but the 3pp spread is short of the 7pp moat bar; returns have been steady (CV 0.25).
It converts 68% of revenue into free cash flow.
As a lender it runs a net interest margin of 1.67% and an efficiency ratio of 70% (cost-heavy).
It earns a 13% return on equity.
hlth: CET1 capital of 11.8% sits comfortably above the ~7% regulatory minimum with buffer.
Non-performing loans are 0.23% of the book, a clean credit profile.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 6.1% over 3 years, 5.8% over 5 years and 5.6% over 10 years.
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 7.6% on average.
Analysts expect 10.3% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.9%), and institutions hold 87%.
Insider trading is two-way: 2 purchases and 3 sales over the past year, net $3.8M sold.
It returns 6.0% a year to shareholders (4.1% in buybacks and 2.0% in dividends).
The share count has shrunk 2.7% a year over five years, steadily raising each holder's stake.
It has paid a dividend for 39 consecutive years.
people: With about 23,800 employees, each generates about $340K of revenue, 0.7x the Financial Services median, and productivity has risen 4.9% a year.
That works out to $229K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $3.8M (11x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
